gauntlet: question
The gathered draft claimed the existing resolver cannot accept overrides. Primary code disproves that claim: `settings/resolver.ts:11` already accepts a timeout override, and every caller I traced reads settings through that resolver. The design will treat the resolver as the single settings boundary unless you say otherwise. The missing timeout override is therefore not a capability gap. The likely root cause is that the existing caller never passes its override to the resolver. A second settings file would add a parallel read path beside the boundary that already owns this setting, so I am raising a framing concern before any other question.

A) as framed - add a second settings file that supplies the timeout override.
B) pivot: change the existing caller to pass its timeout override through `settings/resolver.ts` - this fixes the root cause on the one boundary every caller already uses (`settings/resolver.ts:11`), with no duplicate settings path.
C) smaller or none: document how to set the timeout through the existing resolver and ship no code change. If nothing ships, the override remains silently ignored for that caller.
Recommendation: B - the resolver already supports the override, so fixing the caller removes the bug without creating a second settings boundary.
